The Spigot/Paper/Bukkit entry point. The scripts in `plugins/CraftyTML/ui` are not run on enable, the way a client runs its ui folder: a server has many players, so a script runs for one of them at a time, with that player in its scope as `player`, and the tree it builds is shown to them alone.

- `/ctml run <script> [player]` runs a script for a player and shows what it builds.
- `/ctml demo [player]` shows the intro, and the full demo from it.
- `/ctml close [player]` puts a window away, and `/ctml list` names the scripts.

A script's callbacks are answered by java, the same as on a client. A plugin registers them for a script by name with `callbacks`, and they are put on the context every time that script is opened for a player, from the command or from `open`, with that player to hand. The Paper and Spigot page of the tutorial walks through it.

```java
import net.tutla.craftytml.paper.CraftytmlPaper;
```

## Members

### `public static CTMLWindows windows()`

The windows, for another plugin to open a tree with.

### `public static DOMTreeElement run(Player player, String script)`

Runs a script in the ui folder for one player and hands back the tree it builds, or null where there is no such script or it builds nothing. The script sees the player as `player`.

### `public static void callbacks(String script, BiConsumer<Player, DOMContext> callbacks)`

Callbacks for a script, put on the context of every window that script is opened in. Registered more than once, they are all put on, in the order they were registered.

### `public static boolean open(Player player, String script)`

Runs a script for a player and opens what it builds in front of them, with the callbacks registered for it. Says false where there is no such script or it builds nothing.
